texts.preamble: Kamal Narayan Verma vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 12 October, 2022 1 Nafr High Court Of Chhattisgarh, Bilaspur Crr No. 30 of 2014
texts.arguments: 2. Mr. Yogesh Pandey, learned counsel for the applicant submits that in the case of N. Sukumaran Nair vs Food Inspector, Mavelikara, (1997) 9 SCC 101 in the similar situation Hon'ble Supreme Court has directed the State Government for taking appropriate steps for commutation of the sentence on deposit of Rs.6,000/- in terms of Clause (d) of Section 433 of the Cr.P.C. He further submitted that in the present case the applicant who was not a manufacturer of red lentils ( elwj nky) and he was only selling it in his grocery shop and the same was found adulterated. He further submits that the complaint case was filed on 26-08-2003 and he was convicted by the learned trial Kamal Narayan Verma vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 12 October, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7341284/ 1 Court on 03-11-2012, and appeal preferred by him was dismissed on 06-01-2014 and thus, he is facing trial since 2003. 3. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State submits that the applicant was running a grocery shop from where red lentils ( elwj nky) and tea leaves were purchased by the Food Inspector. The samples taken from the grocery shop were sent for analysis, red lentils (elwj nky) was found adulterated. He further submits that the prosecution has proved guilt of the present applicant beyond reasonable doubt and there is concurrent finding recorded by both the Courts below. 5. Hon'ble Supreme Court while dealing with similar issue in the case of N. Sukumaran Nair vs Food Inspector, Mavelikara (supra) has observed in para 3 as under:- "3.. The offence took place in the year 1984. Under Clause (d) of Section 433 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, "the appropriate government" is empowered to commute the sentence of simple imprisonment for fine. 6. Considering the fact that the complaint case was filed in the year 2003, the applicant is not a manufacturer of the red lentils ( elwj nky), he is facing trial since 2003, therefore, ratio laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of N. Sukumaran Nair vs Food Inspector, Mavelikara (supra) can be applied in the present case.
